1. Introduction
The Precambrian Qaidam-Qilian block (QQB), Altyn Tagh block (ATB) and Tarim block (TB) occupy a large
area in northwestern China, surrounded by Phanerozoic orogenic belts or regional strike-slip faults (Figure 1a).
Their paleogeographic affiliations with the north China craton (NCC) and their positions in the Rodinia super-
continent are intensively debated. One group of ideas places the TB, ATB, and QQB in between Australia and
Laurentia in Rodinia (Lu et al., 2008; Wen et al., 2017, 2018; Xu et al., 2015), and Wen et al. (2018) recently
suggested that a large transform fault along the tentative boundary across the central TB-ATB-QQB promoted
the final assembly of Rodinia by ∼900 Ma. However, this model is challenged by loosely constrained Neoprote-
rozoic TB-ATB-QQB linkage (Song & Li, 2019), and a recent paleomagnetic study from the northern TB (Zhao
et al., 2021) which unraveled a profound paleolatitudinal difference between the north Tarim block (NTB) and
south Tarim block (STB) at ∼900 Ma. Alternatively, other models include the proximities of the TB, ATB, and
QQB with the NCC during the Rodinian era (Pang et al., 2021; Wu et al., 2021; Zuza & Yin, 2017), but are
limited to geological considerations. In this study, we report the new paleomagnetic, geochronological and
geochemical results obtained from 16 mafic dikes in the northern ATB (Figure 1a). The new data, along with
other coeval poles from the NTB, STB, and NCC, and available geological evidence, permits a new contiguous
paleogeographic configuration among the STB, ATB-QQB, and NCC at the northwestern side of Laurentia along
© 2023. American Geophysical Union.
All Rights Reserved. the periphery of Rodinia between ∼895 and ∼780 Ma.

### page_2
Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth 10.1029/2022JB024821
2. Geological Setting and Sampling
The ATB is situated between the TB and the QQB, NW China, bounded to the north and south by the Pale-
ozoic Dunhuang orogen and the Paleo-Mesozoic Kunlun orogen, and to the west and east by the Cenozoic
Qiemo-Mingfeng and Altyn Tagh faults (Figure 1a). Traditionally, the ATB was considered a part of the TB in
Precambrian (e.g., Lu et al., 2008). However, stronger tectonic correlations between the ATB and the QQB are
supported by a growing body of recent geological investigations. After the restoration of ∼400 km displacement
along the Altyn Tagh fault, the ATB together with the QQB, formed a coherent tectonic unit in Precambrian
time (Song & Li, 2019; Zuza & Yin, 2017). Similar Neoproterozoic tectono-thermal activity is widely docu-
mented across the ATB and the QQB, including ∼1000-900 Ma metamorphism, ∼1030-850 Ma arc magma-
tism and ∼850-620 Ma rift-related magmatism (Hao et al., 2020; Peng et al., 2019; Zuza & Yin, 2017). The
Archean-Paleoproterozoic basement is well exposed in the northern ATB and the northern Qaidam block, known
as Milan Complex and Delingha Complex, respectively (Figure 1a). Both underwent ∼2000-1900 Ma metamor-
phism and were intruded by ∼1850 Ma mafic dikes (Lu et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2014), showing similar early
Precambrian geological history among these regions. In addition, recent geochronological studies of the Precam-
brian sedimentary rocks, mainly exposed in the Central-Southern ATB and Qilian block, reveal consistent detri-
tal zircon signature with ∼1300-900 Ma maximum deposition ages, abundant ∼1800-1300 Ma ages and minor
Archean-Paleoproterozoic ages (Figure 1a; Hao, 2021; Li et al., 2020; Wu et al., 2017) suggesting there had been
likely coherency between the Precambrian sedimentary basins.
Our sampling region is located in the northern part of the ATB, where Archean-Paleoproterozoic high-grade
metamorphic basement rocks dominate, here referred to as North Altyn Tagh terrane (NAT) (Figure 1b; Zhang
et al., 2014). Recent studies identified numerous mafic dikes in the NAT, which have different geological features
and ages. One type is apparently altered, which has been dated at 1867 ± 8 Ma (Figure 1b; zircon, U-Pb laser
ablation inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometer (LA-ICPMS) method; Zhang et al., 2014), while another
type is quite fresh in outcrops and thin sections, and has been dated at 884.6 ± 4.2 Ma (Figures 1b and 2; zircon,
U-Pb LA-ICPMS method; Zuo & Long, 2022). The fresh dikes can be further subdivided based on field obser-
vations and petrographic features. We have identified three groups in the region (Figure 1b). The first group
includes many wider (>5 m in width) diabase dikes, showing NW trends (Figures 2a–2d), medium-grained,
being composed of plagioclase (∼50%), clinopyroxene (∼45%) infilled by minor Fe-Ti oxides (Figures 2h–2i).
The second group contains a few significantly narrower (<0.5 m in width) diabase dikes, showing E-W trends
and ophitic texture (Figures 2e and 2j). The third group consists of lamprophyre dikes (Figures 2f–2g), varying
in trends, being composed of hornblende (∼45%), plagioclase (∼40%), clinopyroxene (∼10%) and Fe-Ti oxides
(Figures 2k–2m).
In this study, 147 paleomagnetic core samples were drilled from eight NW-trending diabase dikes, and 25 samples
from three E-W trending diabase dikes, 42 samples from five lamprophyre dikes (Figure 1b). Other 33 core
samples from the gneissic host rocks were collected for baked-contact tests. All the core samples were oriented
using both a magnetic compass and a sun compass. The orientation differences between the two methods are
generally not more than 1°, indicating there is no significant local magnetic anomaly. All sampled dikes are verti-
cal or sub-vertical and fresh in the outcrops. Twelve representative dikes were sampled for geochemical analyses,
including four NW-trending diabase dikes (AT01, 02, 13 and 14), three E-W trending diabase dikes (AT03-05),
and five lamprophyre dikes (AT07-09 and 11–12). Four block samples were further collected from dikes AT01,
02, 13, and 14 for geochronological analyses.
3. Laboratory Techniques
3.1. Geochronology
Sufficient baddeleyite grains were obtained from the samples of dike AT01 (of the first group) through use of
conventional density and magnetic separation. They were mounted in an epoxy resin mount, together with the
Phalaborwa baddeleyite standards (Heaman, 2009). The mount was polished to expose the inside of the badde-
leyite grains. Transmitted and reflected light micrographs, and cathodoluminescence (CL) images were used to
examine the internal structures of the grains, in order to determine the appropriate points for in situ measure-
ments. U-Pb isotopic analyses of the baddeleyite were undertaken on a sensitive high-resolution ion microprobe
(SHRIMP) instrument at the Beijing SHRIMP Centre, China Academy of Geological Sciences, following the

Figure 1. (a) Outline of the northwestern China blocks showing tectonic boundaries and the Precambrian outcrops (modified from Song & Li, 2019). (b) Simplified
geological map of the North Altyn Tagh terrane (modified from Zuo & Long, 2022), showing the sampled NW-trending diabase dikes (golden lines), E-W trending
diabase dikes (blue lines), and lamprophyre dikes (green lines).
method described in Williams (1998). The diameter of the analytical ion beam used is about 25 μm. Standard
baddeleyite Phalaborwa was used to calibrate the Pb/U ratio and U concentration in the target baddeleyites. All
data were processed using the Isoplot/Ex v. 4.15 program (Ludwig, 2012). Analytical errors for individual anal-
ysis in the data table (Table S1 in Supporting Information S1) are at 1σ level, whereas errors for weighted mean
ages are quoted at 2σ level.
3.2. Paleomagnetism
The oriented paleomagnetic core samples were cut into 2.2-cm-long cylindrical specimens. In order to better
understand the magnetic mineralogy and properties of remanence, rock magnetic experiments were conducted.
Thermal demagnetization of triaxial isothermal remanent magnetization (IRM) (Lowrie test; Lowrie, 1990) was
performed for representative specimens which were magnetized in turn along the Z, Y, and X axes in fields of 2.4,
0.4, and 0.12 T, and then underwent stepwise thermal demagnetization up to 690°C. Magnetic hysteresis loop
parameters, including saturation magnetization (Ms), saturation remanence (Mrs), coercive force (Hc) and coer-
civity of remanence (Hcr), were measured for representative specimens through use of a Lakeshore 8600 Vibrat-
ing Sample Magnetometer installed at the Key Laboratory of Paleomagnetism and Tectonic Reconstruction of
Ministry of Natural Resources, CAGS, Beijing. All specimens were applied to stepwise thermal demagnetization
in an ASC TD-48 furnace, the internal residual field in which is less than 10 nT. Nearly half of the parallel spec-
imens were subjected to the alternating field (AF) demagnetization. Remanence was measured using an AGICO
JR-6A spinner magnetometer for most specimens, and a 2G Enterprises 755-4K cryogenic magnetometer for the
specimens with weak natural remanent magnetization intensities (<1 × 10 −3 A/m). All the demagnetizations were
carried out in a low residual magnetic field (<200 nT) shield room at the Paleomagnetism and Environmental
Magnetism Laboratory in China University of Geosciences, Beijing. Magnetic components were determined

Figure 3. The baddeleyite U-Pb dating results of dike AT01. (a) Selected cathodoluminescence images and U-Pb concordia
diagram of baddeleyite grains. (b) 207Pb/ 206Pb age plot of baddeleyite grains. The orange circles on baddeleyite grains
represent the locations of sensitive high-resolution ion microprobe analyses (25 × 25 μm). The solid ellipses represent
concordant data, and the hollow ellipses are discordant data. MSWD, mean square of the weighted deviations.
through use of the principal component analysis (Kirschvink, 1980). The mean directions were calculated using
Fisher statistics (Fisher, 1953). The software packages of Enkin (1990) and Cogné (2003) were used to analyze
the paleomagnetic data.
3.3. Geochemistry
The geochemical samples were crushed and pulverized to 200-mesh in an agate mortar. Major element oxides
were measured by X-ray fluorescence spectrometry (XRF, PW4400) with relative standard deviations <0.5%.
Powdered samples were completely dissolved in high-pressure Teflon bombs using a super-pure HF-HNO3
mixture for 48 hr at ∼100°C. The trace-element concentrations of the samples were determined through use of
an inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS, PE300D). Duplicate analyses of samples and rock
standards yielded relative standard deviations of <5% for most trace elements. All the whole-rock geochemical
analyses were carried out at the National Research Center for Geoanalysis, Chinese Academy of Geological
Sciences (CAGS), Beijing.
4. Results
4.1. Geochronological Results
The baddeleyite grains are tabular, with lengths of 50–80 μm and widths of 30–50 μm (Figure 3a). They
show deep color or parallel striation, without a rim of polycrystalline metamorphic zircon in the CL images
(Figure 3a). Eighteen spots, one spot on each baddeleyite grain, were analyzed. The 18 analyses yielded a
weighted mean 207Pb/ 206Pb age at 901 ± 17 Ma (2σ; MSWD = 1.5) (Figure 3b), and an upper intercept age at
899 ± 17 Ma (2σ, MSWD = 1.5) (Figure 3a). Ten analyses therein are concordant and defined a concordia age at
895.3 ± 7.7 Ma (2σ, MSWD = 0.12) (Table S1 in Supporting Information S1; Figure 3a). The concordia age is
more precise, not influenced by any “crystal orientation effect” (Wingate & Compston, 2000) or Pb loss. We thus
consider it as the best estimate for the crystallization age of the dike AT01.
In a recent study, a weighted mean 206Pb/ 238U zircon age at 884.6 ± 4.2 Ma has been reported for a dike close to
our sampled dike AT01 (Figure 1b; Zuo & Long, 2022). The age is identical to the baddeleyite age of dike AT01
within analytical error. The dike also has similar geochemical and structural features to that of the dike AT01,
suggesting both the well-dated dikes are of the first group.
4.2. Rock Magnetic Results
The representative specimens from the NW-trending diabase dikes (of the first group) and the E-W trending
diabase dikes (of the second group) show similar rock magnetic characteristics. Thermal demagnetization
of the triaxial IRM (Lowrie, 1990) shows that the soft component (SC) (0.12 T) is dominant, with two-step

Figure 4. Rock magnetic results of representative samples. (a–c) Thermal demagnetization of the three-axis isothermal remanent magnetization. (d–f) Wasp-waisted
magnetic hysteresis loops. (g) Day plot for samples from 12 dikes showing their PSD domain magnetite and poor-titanium titanomagnetite behaviors. Samples from the
NW-trending diabase dikes, the E-W trending diabase dikes, and the lamprophyre dikes are marked as orange, blue, and green, respectively. Mrs, saturation remanence;
Ms, saturation magnetization; Hcr, coercivity of remanence; Hc, coercivity; SD, single-domain; PSD, pseudo-single domain; MD, multidomain.
drops at ∼550°C and ∼580°C (Figures 4a–4b), indicating a major contribution of low-coercivity magnetite and
poor-titanium titanomagnetite in the specimens. The hysteresis loops are wasp-waisted with saturation below
500 mT and low coercivity less than 30 mT (Figures 4d–4e), suggesting the dominance of low-coercivity magnetic
carriers. On the Day plot, the hysteresis data for all analyzed specimens fall into the pseudo-single domain (PSD)
region (Figure 4g; Day et al., 1977). These results collectively demonstrate that the paleomagnetically stable PSD
magnetite and poor-titanium titanomagnetite are the major magnetic carriers of the diabase dikes.
The stepwise thermal demagnetizations of the triaxial IRM (Lowrie, 1990) of the lamprophyre dike specimens
show the domination of SC (0.12 T), but with lower unblocking temperature at ∼560°C (Figure 4c), indicating a
domination of low-coercivity poor-titanium titanomagnetite. The wasp-waisted hysteresis loops show the speci-
mens are saturated below 300 mT with coercivity less than 20 mT (Figure 4f). The ratios of Mrs/Ms and Hcr/Hc
fall in the PSD region of the Day plot (Figure 4g; Day et al., 1977). These rock magnetic properties suggest that
PSD poor-titanium titanomagnetite is the main magnetic carrier of the lamprophyre dike specimens.
4.3. Paleomagnetic Results
4.3.1. The NW-Tending Diabase Dikes (The First Group)
A total of 147 specimens from the eight NW-tending diabase dikes were subjected to the stepwise thermal
demagnetization. Two paleomagnetic components were identified. A SC can be determined below 300°C in most
cases (Figures 5a, 5c–5d, and Figures S2a–S2d in Supporting Information S1). The SC directions in situ are close
to the local geocentric axial dipole field (Figure S3 in Supporting Information S1). It is hence interpreted as the
viscous remanent magnetization (VRM) of the local recent geomagnetic field (RGF; D = 0°, I = 58.5°). A char-
acteristic component (CH) was successfully isolated in steps between ∼450°C and ∼580°C (Figures 5a, 5c–5d,
and Figures S2a–S2d in Supporting Information S1), which are consistent with the rock magnetic results. The
CH directions of the eight dikes point southwest up with moderate inclinations, and yield a mean direction of
D = 123.3°, I = −42.2° (α = 12.1°, n = 8) (Table 1; Figure 6a). The CH can also be isolated between ∼20
95
and ∼70 mT, through use of AF demagnetization (Figure 5b, and Figures S2e–S2f, and Table S2 in Supporting
Information S1), which strongly strengthens its stability. We name the CH of the eight NW-tending diabase dikes
(of the first group) as CH1.
Host rocks of dikes AT01 and AT10, both yielding CH1, were sampled for baked-contact test. The baked gneis-
sic samples were obtained within 0.5 m away from the contact, and the unbaked samples were collected at

parameter for mean direction/pole; α /A , radius of circle of 95% confidence about the mean direction/pole; Plat/Plong, Latitude/Longitude of VGP and mean pole.

dp/dm, semi-axes of elliptical error around the pole at a probability of 95%. CH, characteristic remanence magnetization. The bold values are part of the most important
data of this paper.
a distance of ∼50–100 m away from the contact (Figures 7a–7b). Most gneissic specimens yield a VRM of
the RGF (Figure S4 in Supporting Information S1) as the SC of remanence. Three baked specimens of dike
AT01 and four baked specimens of dike AT10 yield a CH, determined between 500°C and 580°C, being simi-
lar to CH1 (Figures 7d–7e and 7g–7h). Unfortunately, the CH directions of the unbaked specimens distribute
randomly (Figures 7g and 7h). We considered that the results partially passed a baked-contact test, supporting
the interpretation that the CH1 is a primary thermal remanent magnetization acquired during dike emplacement
at ∼895 Ma.
A mean paleomagnetic pole (40.9°S, 184.6°E, A = 11.7°) was calculated by averaging the eight virtual
95
geomagnetic poles (VGPs) of each dike (Figure 6c; Table 1). Both the N-dependent A envelope and the 95
scatter of the VGPs were calculated to evaluate the paleosecular variation (PSV). The A falls within an
95
N-dependent A envelope (5.22°, 22.12°) at the 95% confidence interval (Deenen et al., 2011, 2014), and 95
the S of the eight VGPs is 16.7° with 95% confidence interval of (13.4°, 20.0°), which overlaps the excepted
B
range of (10.1°, 14.8°) based on the PSV model for 1.0–2.2 Ga period, while is slightly larger than the
excepted range from 11.1° to 13.2° according to the PSV model for 0.5–1.5 Ga (reference point at 39.2°N,
92.2°E with a paleolatitude of 26.0°) (Smirnov et al., 2011; Veikkolainen & Pesonen, 2014). The results
suggest that the pole is free of PSV influence. In addition, the average pole has no similarity to any younger
paleomagnetic poles in the region. Overall, the new pole of CH1 satisfies six of the seven-point paleomag-
netic data quality criteria (Meert et al., 2020) and can be considered as a high-quality pole of the ATB at
∼895 Ma.

95
4.3.2. The E-W Tending Diabase Dikes (The Second Group)
A total of 25 specimens from the three E-W trending diabase dikes underwent stepwise thermal demagnetization.
Their demagnetization behaviors are similar to those of the specimens from the NW-trending diabase dikes. An
SC was defined below 300°C, and a CH was defined between ∼450°C and ∼580°C (Figure 5e and Figures S2g
and S2h in Supporting Information S1). The SC also represents a recent VRM. The CH directions, however, point
northwest down with significant shallower inclinations (Table 1; Figure 6a). The compatible CH could be isolated
from the parallel specimens between ∼30 and ∼80 mT by AF demagnetization (Table S2 in Supporting Informa-
tion S1; Figure 5f). Because it is obviously distinct from CH1, we name it CH2, representing the paleomagnetic
signal of the E-W trending diabase dikes (of the second group) we sampled.
Three VGPs corresponding to each dike with CH2 were also calculated (Figure 6c; Table 1). However, they are
insufficient to average out the PSV and thus will not be used further for the paleogeographic interpretation.
4.3.3. The Lamprophyre Dikes (The Third Group)
A total of 42 specimens from the five lamprophyre dikes were subjected to thermal demagnetization. An SC
similar to the RGF (Figure S3 in Supporting Information S1) can be removed below 300°C. A CH was identi-
fied between ∼450°C and ∼560°C (Figures 5g–5h and Figures S2j and S2l in Supporting Information S1). The
CH could be also isolated by the AF demagnetization between ∼40 and ∼120 mT (Table S2, Figures S2i, and
S2k in Supporting Information S1). The unblocking temperature and coercivities of the CH are in line with the
rock magnetic analyses (in Section 4.2). The CH directs southeast with shallow to moderate upward inclinations
(Table 1; Figure 6b), which differs from CH1 or CH2 of the diabase dikes. We name it CH3, representing the
paleomagnetic signals of the lamprophyre dikes. Due to the small number of the dikes studied, only five VGPs of
each dike were calculated (Table 1, Figure 6c). They cannot average out the PSV too.
We also collected the gneissic host rock samples of the dike AT11 (∼1-m-wide) within 0.5 m and at >8 m away
from the dike's margin (Figure 7c) for baked contact test. The host rock specimens record an SC likely being the
VRM of RGF (Figure S4 in Supporting Information S1), but yield scattered CH directions (Figure 7i). The results
suggest that the host rocks were not affected by the narrower lamprophyre dike.
4.4. Geochemical Results
The whole-rock major and trace elements compositions of four CH1-bearing diabase dikes, three CH2-bearing
diabase dikes and five CH3-bearing lamprophyre dikes are summarized in Table S3 in Supporting Information S1.

The major and trace elements concentrations show no obvious correlation with the loss on ignition (Figure S1
in Supporting Information S1), suggesting the chemical compositions of analyzed samples are not affected by
weathering or alteration.
The CH1-bearing diabase dikes have a narrow range of SiO (46.48–48.56 wt.%), variable FeO T
2 2 3
(10.51–13.34 wt.%), TiO (1.24–3.21 wt.%) and MgO (6.24–8.12 wt.%) with Mg# values from 48.14 to 57.82. In
2
the chondrite-normalized rare earth element plots, the samples display slightly enriched light rare earth element
(LREE; chondrite-normalized La/Yb = 2.61–3.07) and weakly depleted heavy rare earth element (HREE;
chondrite-normalized Gd/Yb = 1.66–1.85), which are similar to those of the ocean island basalts (OIB) to the
enriched-mid ocean ridge basalts (E-MORB) (Figure 8a). In the primitive mantle-normalized multi-element
spider plots, they show enrichment in Ba, U, Ta, and Zr concentrations, without pronounced negative Nb, Ta,
and Ti anomalies (Figure 8b). The Th/Nb and TiO/Yb ratios range from 0.087 to 0.15, and 0.66 to 0.76, falling
2
into the MORB-ocean plateau basalt-OIB array on the Th/Yb versus Nb/Yb and TiO/Yb versus Th/Nb plots, 2
suggestive of an asthenospheric mantle source without apparent crustal input (Figure 9; Pearce et al., 2021). Our
geochemical analyses of the CH1-bearing diabase dikes are consistent with the dated 884.6 ± 4.2 Ma diabase
dike newly published in the same region (Zuo & Long, 2022), but show distinct geochemical features to the
CH2-bearing diabase dikes and the CH3-bearing lamprophyre dikes.

### page_12
Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth 10.1029/2022JB024821
5. Discussion
5.1. Three Groups of the Sampled Dikes in the Northern ATB
Our geological investigations, paleomagnetic and geochemical analyses consistently indicate that the sampled
16 dikes can be divided into three groups. Group one, which contains the eight NW-trending diabase dikes
with CH1, is characterized by consistent OIB-E-MORB-like REE and multi-element spider patterns with an
asthenospheric mantle source, and is dated at 895.3 ± 7.7 Ma (baddeleyite SHRIMP U-Pb method, this study).
Group two, which comprises the three E-W trending diabase dikes with CH2, is characterized by obvious nega-
tive Nb-Ta-Ti anomalies and an SZLM-dominated source. Group three is composed of the five lamprophyre
dikes with CH3, showing OIB-like features and an asthenospheric mantle source with a large contribution of
deep-recycled crustal materials.
In large scale comparison, the group one dikes are geochemically similar to the ∼890 Ma Chulan-Dalian-Sariwon-Xu-
huai mafic sills in the NCC (Peng et al., 2011 and references therein; Zhang, Zhao, et al., 2016), and the ∼890 Ma
Sailajiazitage basalts in the STB (Figures 8 and 9; Zhang, Li, et al., 2019). If there was then paleogeographic
proximity among the ATB, NCC and STB, the group one dikes could be correlated with the ∼890 Ma large igne-
ous province (LIP) in the NCC and STB. However, the second-group diabase dikes and the lamprophyre dikes
need further direct age constraints.
5.2. The Position of the Northwestern China Blocks in the Periphery of Rodinia
The new ∼895 Ma pole places the sampling site (39.2°N, 92.2°E) at a paleolatitude of 26.0° ± 11.7°, confining
the ATB to low latitudes, which is comparable to the coeval paleolatitudes of the NCC indicated by the paleo-
magnetic pole of the ∼890 Ma mafic sills in the eastern NCC (Fu et al., 2015; Zhao et al., 2020) and that of the
STB constrained by the ∼890 Ma pole of the Sailajiazitage volcanics (Wen et al., 2018). Through matching these
three high-quality poles, and adopting the recent paleogeographic model of NCC-NW Laurentia connection in
Rodinia (Ding et al., 2020, 2021; Fu et al., 2015; Zhao et al., 2020, 2022), we herein propose a paleomagnetic
best-fit location for the ATB that was in between the NCC and STB: the present eastern margin of the ATB facing
the NCC's present western margin, and the present western side of the ATB being close to the STB (Figure 10a).
Both the ATB and STB were attached on the NW Laurentia side of the Rodinia supercontinent together with the
NCC, with the present northern margin of the STB facing an open ocean. Considering the tight tectonic correla-
tions among the ATB and QQB, we suppose the entire ATB-QQB was sandwiched between the NCC and STB
(Figure 10a).
Although paleogeographic interpretation of the new paleomagnetic data has the hemispherical ambiguity and
the paleolongitudinal uncertainty, our model that emphasizes the proximity of the STB, ATB-QQB, and NCC,
can be supported by the following geological correlations: (a) Contiguous early Paleozoic-Mesozoic geological
records across the TB, ATB-QQB, and NCC after the restoration of Cenozoic deformation, suggesting these
blocks were linked by at least the early Paleozoic (Zuza & Yin, 2017). (b) Highly similar upper Neoproterozoic
lithostratigraphic sequence of the Qaidam block and NCC, which is marked by the post-Gaskiers glaciation, and
the overlying siliciclastic depositions with the Ediacara-type fossil Shaanxilithes (Pang et al., 2021 and references
therein). (c) Shared synchronous Neoproterozoic LIP fragments (e.g., the ∼890 Ma LIPs across the ATB-QQB,
NCC, and the STB, Peng et al., 2011; Zhang, Zhao, et al., 2016; Zhang, Li, et al., 2019; Zuo & Long, 2022).
Both the ATB-QQB and NCC recorded two other phases of LIPs, including ∼850-820 Ma LIP with consistent
OIB-E-MORB type compositions formed in intraplate settings (e.g., the 846-821 Ma Yingfeng mafic dikes in
the northern Qaidam block, Lu et al., 2008; Xu et al., 2016; the ∼825 Ma Jinchuan mafic-ultramafic rocks and
the ∼830 Ma Luanchuan gabbro in the NCC, Li et al., 2005; Wang et al., 2011), and ∼780 Ma LIP sourced from
enriched mantle with contamination of continental crust (e.g., the ⁓780 Ma meta-mafic volcanics in the northern
Qaidam block, Peng et al., 2019; the ∼775 Ma Lulong mafic dikes in the NCC, Ding et al., 2021). (d) Comparable
late Paleoproterozoic-Mesoproterozoic cover sequence and Paleoproterozoic magmatic-metamorphic events: the
late Mesoproterozoic Tuolai Group in the Qilian block and the Suoerkuli Group in the ATB could be equivalent
to the Dunzigou Group in the southwestern NCC and the Baiyinbaolage Formation in the northern NCC, based
on similar detrital zircon age populations (Wu et al., 2021). The recently revised <1730-1640 Ma rift to passive
margin strata in the northern Qaidam block—Quanji Group can be correlative with the Changcheng Group in the
NCC (Wang et al., 2022; Zhang, Wang, et al., 2016), and the ∼1500 Ma Sangzhutage Group in the southwestern

Figure 10. Paleogeographic reconstruction of Rodinia. (a) ∼890 Ma reconstruction. The partnership among the south Tarim block (STB), Altyn Tagh block (ATB)
and north China craton (NCC) is based on the fit of three coeval poles from each block. Blocks and their poles (listed in Table 2) are matched in color. The NCC-NW
Laurentia connection is based on Ding et al. (2021). The baltica-1 position is adopted from the “right-way-up” model (Cawood & Pisarevsky, 2006). The baltica-2
position is based on the fit of new 900 Ma pole (“Bal900”; Kulakov et al., 2022) with the pole “NC890.” The “tight fit” between Siberia and Laurentia is adopted
from Evans et al. (2016). (b) ∼780 Ma reconstruction. The relationship between the STB-ATB-QQB, NCC, and Laurentia at ∼780 Ma is same as that of (a) (based
on the poles “NC775,” “Lau775,” and “TB760” in Table 2), in the case of the Tarim block (TB) was united at this time. The plume centers are inferred from fitting
∼780 Ma mafic dikes/volcanics around the TB-QQB-Siberia, and NCC-Laurentia, respectively. Parameters of the Euler rotation are listed in Table S4 in Supporting
Information S1.
STB shares the same passive margin rock assemblage with that of the NCC as well (Zhang, Ye, et al., 2019).
Moreover, both ∼1900 Ma metamorphism and ∼1800 Ma extensional magmatism had been widely reported from
the southwestern STB, ATB-QQB, and NCC (Lu et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2014; Zhang, Ye, et al., 2019; Zhang
et al., 2021 and references therein).
Our model places the ATB-QQB next to the present western margin of Siberia craton (Figure 10a), if we adopt
the “tight fit” model of the Laurentia-Siberia connection in Rodinia (e.g., Ernst et al., 2016; Evans et al., 2016).
It does make sense from several geological observations available. Similar middle Neoproterozoic intraplate
magmatism had been identified from both continents, that is, the ∼790 Ma mafic dikes in the Yenisey Ridge
(Likhanov & Santosh, 2017) and the ∼780 Ma meta-mafic volcanic rocks in the northern Qaidam block (Peng
et al., 2019). The recently revealed Grenville-aged (∼1100-900 Ma) granitoid and metamorphic rocks in both the
Yenisey Ridge (Likhanov et al., 2014) and the ATB-QQB (Peng et al., 2019; Song et al., 2012) may represent the
late Mesoproterozoic to early Neoproterozoic convergence between western Siberia and the ATB-QQB.
Our reconstruction indicates that the western Laurentia along with the NCC, ATB-QQB, and STB were located in
low latitudes at ∼890 Ma (Figure 10a). It is also paleomagnetically permitted to place the STB on the outboard of
western Laurentia; however, whether it was connected with Australia craton (Wen et al., 2018) is unclear because
there is no coeval paleomagnetic pole from Australia. Recent paleomagnetic results from the Qigelekekuotan
volcanics in the northern TB revealed considerably higher paleolatitudes of the NTB at ∼900 Ma (Zhao
et al., 2021), excluding its neighborhood relationship with western Laurentia. In conclusion, it is unlikely that a
united TB played a linkage role between Australia and Laurentia (Wen et al., 2017, 2018) at ∼900 Ma.
The reconstruction model can also be valid at ∼780 Ma (Figure 10b), when the STB and NTB were likely
united as one tectonic unit—TB (Zhang, Ye, et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2021; Zhao et al., 2021). Three ∼770 Ma
paleomagnetic poles (TB760, NC775, and Lau775; Table 2) can support the same paleogeographic relation-
ship between the STB and NCC as that in our ∼890 Ma model. Both the middle Neoproterozoic plume-related

magmatism in the northern China blocks, including the ∼800-760 Ma Quruqtagh and Aksu dikes in the TB
(Zhang et al., 2009), the ∼780 Ma meta-mafic volcanics in northern Qaidam block (Peng et al., 2019), and the
∼775 Ma Lulong dikes in the NCC (Wang et al., 2016) sourced from the SZLM, and the ∼790 Ma Yenisey
dikes along western Siberia with intraplate basalt geochemistry (Likhanov & Santosh, 2017), are compara-
ble with that of the ∼775 Ma Gunbarrel dikes along western Laurentia (Mackinder et al., 2019 and references
therein). The geometry of these dike swarms could constitute the contemporary LIPs in western Laurentia and
the NCC-ATB-QQB-TB (Figure 10b).
Some researchers also speculated on a long-lived proximity of the northwestern China blocks and NCC with
Baltica (Zuza & Yin, 2017), based on the geological similarities among these blocks. The STB, ATB-QQB, and
NCC, however, were located at low paleolatitudes at ∼890 Ma, while the ∼950-870 Ma paleomagnetic poles
(Bal951-935, Bal900, Bal870; Table 2) place Baltica in significantly higher paleolatitudes. The current paleo-
magnetic data do not support a model that Baltica was close to the STB, ATB-QQB, and NCC, but they can be
placed on the opposite sides of Laurentia instead (Figure 10a; Fu et al., 2015).
6. Conclusions
A new paleomagnetic pole was obtained from eight NW-trending diabase dikes in the northern ATB. One of
the dikes was newly dated at ∼895 Ma through use of baddeleyite U-Pb SHRIMP methodology. The new data
together with global paleomagnetic database and aided by geological evidence, suggest that the neighboring STB,
ATB-QQB and NCC were located along the NW side of Laurentia in Rodinia at ∼895 Ma. The connection might
be valid until ∼780 Ma.
